headline.en: The simplest harmony: sing the tune's next chord tone up. Mostly that's a third; over so it's a fourth, because the third would rub.

detail.en: One line, the tune and the part above together

title.en: Sing the tune, then the part

detail.en: Every harmony note lit
You'll hear the tune as you sing

text.en: Hold the harmony on the long notes while the tune moves. Hear the chord ring.
Now sing the tune itself, once through, so it's yours.
Now the part above, the whole verse, every note lit, while the guide sings the tune.

measures.en: Your stars are for your harmony's notes on pitch. You sang parallel thirds, with a fourth wherever the third would rub.

headline.en: A third above switches between major and minor to stay in the key. You don't count it: you follow the scale, two notes up.

detail.en: Do to mi, fa to la, so to ti
Re to fa, mi to so
Listen to them under you

text.en: Listen to each, as often as you like, then choose the third that fits.

prompt.en: Over do, which third fits the key?

why.en: A, do to mi, is a major third, in the key. B's note is a half step low: it clashes with the chord.

prompt.en: Over re, which third fits the key?

why.en: B, re to fa, is a minor third: smaller, but in the key. A's note is outside it.

prompt.en: Over mi, which third fits the key?

why.en: A, mi to so, a minor third, stays in the key. A third above isn't always the same size.

prompt.en: Over fa, which third fits the key?

why.en: B, fa to la, a major third. The key decides: you just follow the scale.

text.en: The guide climbs do re mi fa so; you sing a third above each, over the chords.

measures.en: Your stars are for your thirds on pitch, major and minor.

headline.en: Over so, the third above is ti, and ti rubs against the chord of do. So the part goes up a fourth, to do.

detail.en: Not ti, but do
The next note in the chord
Row, boat, shore, jah

text.en: Listen to each, then choose the one that rubs.

why.en: A puts ti over the chord of do: a seventh against do, and it rubs. B's do rings.
B's ti rubs again. Over so, take do: a fourth up, in the chord.

text.en: The first line again, the part above: do over every so.

measures.en: Your stars are for your harmony's notes on pitch, every so answered with do.

headline.en: A harmony makes chords with the tune; a copy just doubles it. Learn to hear the difference, then keep your part as the lights fade.

detail.en: Harmony, or the same tune?
The whole verse
The second half is yours, by ear

text.en: Listen to each, as often as you like, then choose.

prompt.en: Is the second voice singing a harmony, or the same tune?

why.en: A harmony: the second voice moved with the tune but on its own notes, a chord tone above.

prompt.en: Is the second voice singing a harmony, or the same tune?

why.en: The same tune, an octave up. It's fuller, but it isn't a harmony: every note is the tune's own.
B copied: the second voice sang the tune's own notes. A made chords.
A copied. Listen for the moment two voices become one: that's a copy.

text.en: The part above, the whole verse. Halfway through, the lights fade: keep going by ear.

measures.en: Your stars are for your harmony's notes on pitch, the second half sung with no lights to follow.

headline.en: A tune you know less: Home on the Range's refrain. The same rule: the next chord tone up, a third over passing notes.

detail.en: Home, home on the range
Between them, by ear
Above a loud tune, go lighter, never louder

text.en: The part above the refrain. The lights show only where the chord changes.

measures.en: Your stars are for your part's notes on pitch, most of them sung with no light to follow.

headline.en: A third above, an octave down, is a sixth below. Under so, sing do, not ti: the same fix, upside down.

detail.en: Michael, Row again
The same notes as the part above, an octave down
Listen up to the tune

text.en: The part below, the whole verse, while the guide sings the tune above you.

measures.en: Your stars are for your part's notes on pitch, under the tune.

headline.en: Lost? Hold your note until it rubs, then step. A rub usually steps, most often down: over the chord of so, do steps to ti.

detail.en: Under Michael's second line
The chord changes to so: step down to ti
Back to do when the chord comes home

text.en: Hold do under the tune; where the chord changes and it rubs, step to ti, then back home.

measures.en: Your stars are for your held notes on pitch, and the step to ti where the chord changed.

headline.en: Hear a line once, then harmonise it as it comes round again: the first step to harmonising a tune you've never heard.

detail.en: The guide sings a line
The line again, you above it
As before, by ear now

text.en: Hear the line; then the guide sings it again and you sing the part above.
The second line: hear it, then harmonise it as it comes round again.

measures.en: Your stars are for your part's notes on pitch as the line came round again.

headline.en: Steal Away, the spiritual's refrain: once with your part below the tune, then once above it.

detail.en: Your part under the tune
The same part, an octave up
Hold your note until it rubs, then step

text.en: The refrain, your part below the tune.
Again, your part above the tune.

measures.en: Your stars are for your part above on pitch. Could you hear the tune under you?

headline.en: A chord has three notes, and any of them is a harmony, except the tune's own.

detail.en: Its three notes, up and back
One long note to each chord
The tune's own note never lights

text.en: Sing each chord's notes, up and back, over its chord.
One long note to each chord: any lit note, under or over the tune.

measures.en: Your stars are for landing on a lit note at each chord, and three need at least three moves against the tune.

headline.en: Two ways to make a part your own: barely move, or move against the tune.

detail.en: A step or less from note to note
When the tune climbs, fall
Hear both together

text.en: Take 1: any lit note, moving as little as you can.

measures.en: Three stars need four moves in five to be a step or less.

text.en: Take 2: any lit note, moving against the tune.

measures.en: Three stars need at least three moves against the tune.

headline.en: Swing Low, Sweet Chariot's chorus, your own harmony: any lit note, the tune's own never.

detail.en: Choose as you go
Small moves make a part easy to sing
Hear it together afterwards

text.en: The chorus: at each note, any lit note. Make your own harmony.

measures.en: Your stars are for landing on lit notes, and three need four moves in five to be a step or less.

headline.en: Fewer lights: they show only where the chord changes. Between, you know where you are.

detail.en: Then hold or step by ear
Hold your note until it rubs, then step
In the chord, never the tune's own

text.en: Michael, Row with lights only at the chord changes.

measures.en: Your stars are for your notes landing in the chord, most of them with no light to follow.

headline.en: No lights at all. The chords sound under you: any note in the chord, except the tune's own, is a harmony.

detail.en: They tell you where you are
Hold a note until it rubs, then step
Hear what you made

text.en: Michael, Row, lights off. Sing a harmony by ear.

measures.en: Your stars are for your notes landing in the chord, by ear.

headline.en: The tenor, a part above the lead, is part of bluegrass's high lonesome sound. Light and easy, never the pressed edge.

detail.en: Every note higher than the lead's
By ear
Never pushed

text.en: Simple Gifts: a part above the tune, lights off.

measures.en: Your stars are for your notes landing in the chord, above the tune.

headline.en: Red River Valley, a tune new to this course. Hear it once; then harmonise it by ear, again, and then a part under your own.

detail.en: Just the tune
Lights off; the second time you know it
Three of you

text.en: First listen: a harmony by ear, lights off.
Again: now you know the tune.
Last: a part under the tune, with your second take singing too. A trio of you.

measures.en: Your stars are for this last part's notes landing in the chord. Hear it together: the tune, and three of you.
